description.narrative:
In a region where securing Sexual and Reproductive Health and Rights (SRHR) is especially challenging, Masarouna will mobilize the power of young people’s collective action in six Middle East and North Africa (MENA) countries to support their fight for greater freedom of choice and respect for their SRHR through new and innovative pathways for change. Our vision is that young people (YP) meaningfully induce sustainable change that will enable them to enjoy their SRHR. Jordan is one of the countries where the Masarouna programme will be implemented.
Context: In 2019, 41.4% of MENA’s population was aged 15-39, making it one of the world’s youngest regions. In recent years, young people have demonstrated their ability to become main drivers for change in response to long-standing structural inequalities, rising authoritarianism and increased levels of conflict and fragility. Young people in MENA continue to facesome of the most vocal conservative opposition to their SRHR. The problem that Masarouna will tackle is the perpetual obfuscation and the increasing weaponization of SRHR as a form of social control. This strips SRHR of the urgency it deserves, yet, we strongly believe fulfilling young people’s SRHR can have a transformative effect on sustainable development due to its connection with basic human well-being and gender equality. Strategic objective: Young people in six selected countries in the MENA region achieve more freedom to enjoy their SRHR in inclusive societies. Targeted group: Young people aged 18-35, in particular (unmarried) women and LGBTQI+. Activists and individuals will be mobilized as agents and drivers of change throughout the programme cycle.
The programme’s strategic objective and outcomes contribute directly to achieving SDGs 3 (health and well-being), 5 (gender equality) and 10 (reduced inequalities. The programme is fully aligned with the ICPD25 Nairobi statement’s call for renewed commitments towards women’s and Young People’s SRHR.
The Masarouna programme implements two main pathways of change:
1: Lobby and advocacy with young people for theirSRHR The first pathway promotes greater accountability of governments to adhere to international SRHR standards, human rights frameworks and agreements; promotes young people’s active and meaningful involvement in policy agenda-setting and decision-making; and increases public awareness on SRHR, including through media engagement, aiming to create new narratives on SRHR.
2: Strengthening civil society and reinventing civic space A strong civilsociety can be a mobilizer, an amplifier of voices and a watchdog. With strengthened capacities, CSOs can create a sense of urgency around SRHR to push for sustainable change. CSOs need the space to play this political role, which Masarouna aims to reinvent by promoting the political activation and participation of young people and creating and strengthening alternative civic spaces, both online and offline. Working online allows for reaching young people at scale by circumventing gatekeepers and mitigating risks around censorship.

participating-org.narrative: Oxfam is an international confederation of 17 organizations working together in more than 90 countries. Oxfam International was formed in 1995 by a group of independent non-governmental organizations. Their aim was to work together for greater impact on the international stage to reduce poverty and injustice. The name ?Oxfam? comes from the Oxford Committee for Famine Relief, founded in Britain in 1942. The group campaigned for food supplies to be sent through an allied naval blockade to starving women and children in enemy-occupied Greece during the Second World War. As well as becoming a world leader in the delivery of emergency relief, Oxfam International implements long-term development programs in vulnerable communities. We are also part of a global movement, campaigning withothers, for instance, to end unfair trade rules, demand better health and education services for all, and to combat climate change.Today, there are 17 member organizations of the Oxfam International confederation. They are based in: Australia, Belgium, Canada, France, Germany, Great Britain, Hong Kong, Ireland, India, Italy, Japan, Mexico, The Netherlands, New Zealand, Quebec, Spain and the United States. The Oxfam International Secretariat is based in Oxford, UK. The Secretariat runs advocacy offices in Brussels, Geneva, New York, Washington DC and Brasilia. Oxfam GB is an actor in the implementation of this project.

description.narrative: KI-6 # Women led CSOs/movements capacitated by Masarouna to advocate for safe and adequate SRHR information and services for diverse young people

comment.narrative: A Mutual Capacity Strengthening (CATool) survey was conducted in 2022. The topics for which organisations joining Masarouna in 2022 expressed a need on capacity strengthening in relation to influencing on SRHR for young people are: developing an influencing strategy; lobby and/or advocacy on SRHR policies and practices; digital campaigning and influencing social norms. Organisations indicated that they are currently supporting others on lobby and/or advocacy on SRHR policies and practices; and digital campaigning. (Organisations could express a need, an offer, or both a need and offer on the same topic.)

In relation to SRHR influencing capacity, based on the criteria agreed on, the women-led Oxfam partner realized an actual for KI-6 in 2023 (against a target in 2024). The partner reported increased capacity on Influencing strategies led by and with diverse young people; and Developing an influencing strategy in 2023. The actual achieved by the partner is reported in IATI for KI-6 in 2023, as this was the first time this partner realized an actual for 1 of the 3 capacity strengthening KIs. In relation toSRHR influencing capacity, based on the criteria agreed on, the women-led RNW Media partner did not realize an actual for KI-6 in 2023 against the target in 2023 as they did not report increased capacity in 2023.

In relation to SRHR influencing capacity, the women-led partner of Oxfam had further improved its capacity in Developing an influencing strategy, and lobby and/or advocacy SRHR policies and practices in 2024. This resulted in an actual for KI-6 in 2024 based on the criteria agreed on. An actual is not reported in IATI as this partner was already counted as an actual in 2023 for 1 of the 3 capacity strengthening KIs [KI-6].

The two new women led RNW Media partners that joined the programme in 2022 did not yet report on their capacity level, however, expressed an interest to (further) increase several capacities related to influencing on SRHR with diverse young people over the course of the programme (see baseline information). There was no target set for KI-6 for these partners in 2022. One of these women led partners ceased to be part of the partnership in the course of 2022.

As a result of capacity strengthening support from RNW Media, partners will improve their capacity in creating engaging SRHR content and establishing safe and adequate digital campaigning on SRHR issues and how to use data for advocacy.

In 2023, Oxfam in country onboarded a women led partner in the MENA region. The new partner will receive capacity strengthening on advocacy in 2024: Capacity strengthening in relation to influencing on SRHR for diverse young people will focus on the needs as expressed by the respective organisations involved in the MENA region. These shall still include capacity strengthening on lobby and/or advocacy on policies and practices, digital campaigning, and developing an influencing strategy. The same will beoffered to CSOs who are not Masarouna contracted partners, for instance some youth-led organisations.

description.narrative: KI-6 # CSOs/movements, both women and youth led, capacitated by Masarouna to advocate for safe and adequate SRHR information and services for diverse young people

comment.narrative: A Mutual Capacity Strengthening baseline survey was conducted in 2021, screening seven different capacities under the topic of influencing and awareness raising on SRHR for young people. These are: developing an influencing strategy, youth-led influencing, lobby and/or advocacy on policies and practices, public campaigning, digital campaigning, working with traditional media, and influencing social norms. The topics for which most of the organizations involved in Masarouna expressed a need on capacity strengthening, are: lobby and/or advocacy on policies and practices, digital campaigning, and developing an influencing strategy. The topics for which most organizations indicated to already having a strong capacity and being able to support others, are: youth-led influencing, public campaigning, developing an influencing strategy, and working with traditional media. (Organisations could express a need, an offer, or both a need and offer on the same topic).

In relation to SRHR influencing capacity, one partner of Oxfam reported increased capacity on Developing an influencing strategy in 2024. An actual is not achieved for this partner based on the agreed on criteria and therefore is not reported in IATI forKI-6 for 2024. Worth mentioning that this partner was already counted as an actual in 2022 for 1 of the 3 capacity strengthening KIs [KI-6]. The other both women and youth led partner of Oxfam did not report increased capacity in relation to SRHR influencing, however, maintained its capacity in 2024. An actual is not achieved for this partner based on the agreed on criteria and is not reported in IATI for KI-6 for 2024 as this partner was already counted as an actual in 2022 for 1 of the 3 capacity strengthening KIs.

In relation to SRHR influencing with diverse young people, two both-women-and-youth-led Oxfam partners reported an increased capacity since joining the programme. Both partners reported increased capacity on developing an influencing strategy and influencing social norms. Based on the criteria agreed on, both organisations realized an actual for KI-6 in 2022 against the target for 2022. The both-women-and-youth-led organisations also expressed an interest to (further) increase several capacities relatedto SRHR influencing with diverse young people over the course of the programme. (Source CATool 2022)

In relation to SRHR/SOGIE influencing capacity, one both women and youth-led Oxfam partner reported increased capacity on Influencing strategies led by and with diverse young people; Public campaigning; Digital campaigning; Working with traditional media; Developing an influencing strategy; and Lobby and/or advocacy SRHR policies and practices in 2023. An actual for this Oxfam partner is not reported in IATI for KI-6 for 2023, as the partner was already counted as an actual in 2022 for 1 of the 3 capacity strengthening KIs [KI-6]. Similarly, the other both women and youth-led Oxfam partner reported increased capacity on Influencing strategies led by and with diverse young people; Public campaigning; Digital campaigning; Influencing social norms; Developing an influencing strategy; and Lobby and/or advocacy SRHR policies and practices in 2023. An actual for the partner is not reported in IATI for KI-6 for 2023, as the partner was already counted as an actual in 2022 for 1 of the 3 capacity strengtheningKIs [KI-6].

Capacity strengthening in relation to influencing on SRHR for diverse young people will focus on the needs as expressed by respective organisations involved in Masarouna. These include capacity strengthening on lobby and/or advocacy on policies and practices, digital campaigning, and developing an influencing strategy. This capacity strengthening will also be offered to CSOs who are not Masarouna contracted partners, for instance some youth-led organisations.

Capacity strengthening in relation to influencing on SRHR for diverse YP will focus on the needs as expressed by the partners involved in Masarouna in the MENA region. The sessions will include capacity strengthening on lobby and/or advocacy on policiesand practices, digital campaigning, and developing an influencing strategy. The same will be offered to CSOs who are not Masarouna contracted partners, for instance some youth-led organisations.

description.narrative: KI-6 # Youth led CSOs/movements capacitated by Masarouna to advocate for safe and adequate SRHR information and services for diverse young people
KI-13 # Women led CSOs/ movements supported by Masarouna to strengthen their civic space influencing capacity

comment.narrative: A Mutual Capacity Strengthening (CATool) survey was conducted in 2022. In relation to civic space influencing capacities, organizations joining Masarouna in 2022 expressed a need for capacity strengthening on understanding and navigating (offline and online) civic space for young people working on SRHR; civic space risk mitigation & protection of staff, partners and people we work with; protection in digital space; health and wellbeing; strengthen/broaden partnerships (movements & coalitions). Partners also indicated to currently support others on: understanding and navigating (offline and online) civic space for young people working on SRHR; health and well-being; perception by and relationship with constituency; and strengthen/broaden partnerships (movements & coalitions).(Organisations could express a need, an offer, or both a need and offer on the same topic)

In relation to civic space influencing capacity, based on the criteria agreed on, the women-led Oxfam partner realized an actual for KI-13 in 2023. This partner reported increased capacity on Understanding and navigating civic space; and Civic space risk mitigation and protection of staff in 2023; resulting in an actual in 2023 against a target in 2024. The actual for prtner is not reported in IATI for KI-13 in 2023, as the partner was already counted as an actual in 2023 for 1 of the 3 capacity strengthening KIs [Ki-6]. In relation to civic space influencing capacity, based on the criteria agreed on, the women-led RNW Media partner did not realize an actual for KI-12 in 2023 against the target in 2023 as they did not report increased capacity in 2023.

In relation to civic space influencing capacity, based on the criteria agreed on, the women-led partner of Oxfam realized an actual for KI-13 in 2024. This partner reported increased capacity on Civic Space risk Mitigation and protection of staff; and on Health and Wellbeing in 2024; resulting in an actual in 2024 based on the criteria agreed on. The actual for this partner is not reported in IATI for KI-13 in 2024, as this organisation was already counted as an actual in 2023 for 1 of the 3 capacity strengthening KIs [KI-6].

The new women led RNW Media partners that joined the programme in 2022 did not yet report on their capacity level, however, expressed an interest to (further) increase several capacities related civic space influencing over the course of the programme (see baseline information). There was no target set for KI-12 for these partners in 2022. One of these women led partners ceased to be part of the partnership in the course of 2022.

As a result of capacity strengthening provided by RNW Media, partners will improve their practices and policies in digital safety and security to be applied in their work on digital campaigning. In addition, they will improve organisational capacity in digital rights and media campaigns for social change. This enables the organisation to use media engagement for changing the civic space and build public awareness.

A new women-led partner was onboarded in 2023 to the project by the Oxfam country office, and will receive capacity strengthening on civic space influencing capacity in 2024. Capacity strengthening in relation to civic space influencing will focus on theneeds as expressed by respective organisations involved in Masarouna in country implementation. These include widening (digital) civic space for young people working on SRHR; protection in digital space; and perception by and relationship with constituency. In addition, Oxfam in country aims to conduct a research on the shrinking civic space around SRHR, mitigation strategies, opportunities, threats. This research will also be used to inform the exit strategy of the project, which will benefit all CSOs working around SRHR, as well as a follow up event on the status of the civic space around SRHR. Based on a follow up on safe programming, new risk mitigation plans may be developed. (This new partner is not included in the target for KI-13/2024 in IATI to avoid double counting with the target reported for this organisations for KI-6 for 2024.)

description.narrative: KI-12 # Women led CSOs/ movements supported by Masarouna to strengthen their organizational capacities

comment.narrative: A Mutual Capacity Strengthening (CATool) survey was conducted in 2022. In relation to organisational capacities, organizations joining Masarouna in 2022 expressed a need for capacity strengthening on Feminist MEAL; safeguarding (prevention); safeguarding(response); project management; and fundraising. They also indicated to currently support others on project (financial) management and fundraising. In relation to x-cutting themes, organizations joining Masarouna in 2022 expressed a need for capacity strengthening on Sexual and Reproductive Health and Rights (SRHR) foundational knowledge; youth engagement practices; transformative leadership; working with specific target groups relevant to the program; and analyse and integrate conflict sensivity. They also indicated to currently support others on the same topics. (Organisations could express a need, an offer, or both a need and offer on the same topic).

In relation to X-cutting and organisational capacity, the women-led Oxfam partner reported increased capacity on SRHR foundational knowledge and Young people engagement practices in 2023, however, this did not result in an actual for KI-12 in 2023 based on the criteria agreed on. (A target for KI-12 has been set for 2024 for this partner). In relation to cross cutting and organisational capacity, based on the criteria agreed on, the women-led RNW media partner did not realize an actual for KI-12 in 2023against the target in 2023 as they did not report increased capacity in 2023.

In relation to x-cutting and organisational capacity, the women-led partner of Oxfam partner reported increased capacity on SRHR foundational knowledge; Project management; Safeguarding: responding to cases of inappropriate behaviour; Working with specific target groups; and Youth engagement practices in 2024. This resulted in an actual for KI-12 in 2024 based on the criteria agreed on. An actual is not reported in IATI as this organisation was already counted as an actual in 2023 for 1 of the 3 capacitystrengthening KIs [KI-6]. The women-led partner of RNW Media did not participate in the CATool in 2024, hence, no updates in 2024.

The new women led RNW Media partners that joined the programme in 2022 did not yet report on their capacity level, however, expressed an interest to (further) increase several capacities related to x-cutting themes and organisational capacity over the course of the programme (see baseline information). There was no target set for KI-12 for these partners in 2022. One of these women led partners ceased to be part of the partnership in the course of 2022.

As a result of close collaboration with RNW Media, partners have strengthened capacities on PMEAL, finance and project management. RNW Media will support on the use of online data collection, analysis and visualisation to all consortium partners. In addition, the organisation will improve their safeguarding policies and practicies; as well as strengthen their organisational capacities in project management and financial management through continuous feedback and support during the implementation course.

In 2023, Oxfam in country onboarded a women led partner in the MENA region. The new partner will receive capacity strengthening on advocacy in 2024. The capacity strengthening will be in relation to organisational capacities based on the needs as expressed by respective partners involved in Masarouna in the MENA region. These includes capacity strengthening on MEAL, in particular feminist MEAL, Outcome Harvesting, and project management training.
Capacity strengthening in relation to cross cutting themes will focus on the needs as expressed by respective partners involved in Masarouna in the MENA region. These include SRHR foundational knowledge, feminist approach to (SRHR) influencing, gender and power analysis, and transformative leadership. (This new partner is not included in the target for KI-12/2024 in IATI to avoid double counting with the target reported for this organisations for KI-6 for 2024.)
As a result of continuous support from RNW Media, The RNW Media partner onboarded will improve their safeguarding policies and practicies; as well as strengthen their organisational capacities in project management through continuous feedback and support during the implementation course. In addition, the partner is taking part in the digital transformation trajectory of RNW Media to identify improvements points to strengthen their organisational and technical capacities related to digital reach and engagement. (A target was already included for this partner in 2023, hence not repeated to avoid duplication).
One women-led partner will engage in fundraising capacity strengthening and developing fundraising strategy in 2025. No quantitative target is set to avoid double counting.

comment.narrative: According to the Mutual Capacity Strengthening baseline survey conducted in 2021, in relation to organisational capacity, the topics for which most of the organizations involved in Masarouna expressed a need on capacity strengthening, are: MEAL, in particular feminist MEAL, and fundraising/proposal writing. KI-1a # Governmental policies blocked, adopted and/or improved to enable diverse young people to enjoy their SRHR

comment.narrative: There is no specific law or policy targeting young people's access to their SRHR; SRHR is not included in the national school curriculum.

The program contributed toward change in policies and laws in the region under the SRHR Influencing Strategy development activity aiming at promoting support from policymakers, influencers, religious leaders, young people, parents, and community leaders to achieve sustainable, policy change and accountability that advances SRHR and gender equality. A workshop was conducted to draft the strategy for the upcoming 3 years with a total of 54 attendees representing various stakeholders including government representatives from the Parliament, Ministries of Health, Education, Culture and Youth, Endowment, Justice, and Higher Education. The Influencing Strategy focused on a number of objectives 1. Age and culturally appropriate and evidence-based comprehensive sex education curriculum (CSE) for high school students be developed and endorsed by the ministry of education by 2025. 2. By 2025, 75% of young people and parents involved in the awareness creation programs in two governorates perceive the SRHR information received as adequate to their specific needs and interests, and they are supportive of SRHR of YP. 3. By 2025, a comprehensive SRHR curriculum is implemented as part of the pre-marital course for couples (PMCC). 4. SRHR units that provide consultation on SRHR for young people and all genders are established and operational in primary healthcare centers in two governorate by 2025. 5. The context and dynamics of honor killing assessed and finding disseminated by end of 2024.

The project will focus on the design, adoption , and implementation (if the conditions allow) of policies/and or laws specifically targeting young people and their SRHR. According to a preliminary analysis conducted in the baseline, (adapted) SRHR information is not included in the school curriculum. Our goal is to launch a process of designing such curriculum, which would be adopted by the Ministry of Education by the end of the project.
Update Oct. 2023: Due to various contextual constraints, it isnot feasible to have at least one governmental policy change by the end of the project. The 5-year target has therefor been adjusted from 1 to zero at midterm. We will however focus on alternative strategies to advance our mission within the current constraints.
